trickyParts: Start point: rebased the plan commit once onto main@origin (1639fb6b, post-#992) before any PR existed. main moved 7 more commits during the work (through 45f33bd8); the two files both sides touch (daemon AGENTS.md, worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md) have non-overlapping hunks, GitHub reports MERGEABLE, so no second rebase.

LEGION_OMP_PATH: on main resolveOmpInvocation read it from the env it was handed, which is paneEnv; under the allow-list paneEnv no longer carries LEGION_*, so the override would have silently stopped working. Split the parameters: daemon env for configuredPath, paneEnv for the mise where call; environment.test.ts pins it.

gh children: createCiStatusFetcher, workerCatchup and GitHubService spread buildRoleEnv(..., process.env) over the runner's paneEnv - the whole daemon environment incl. the keys. Now every one takes baseEnv (required, no default) = environment.paneEnv.

Scrub semantics verified on a scratch tmux 3.7c server: `set-environment -g -u` removes the entry (absent from show-environment -g), `-r` leaves a -NAME marker; both keep the name out of a subsequently created pane (verified via /proc/<pane pid>/environ). Used -u. -u on a missing name exits 0 and creates no marker; -u on a BASH_FUNC_x%% name works.

tmux itself writes PWD and SHLVL into the global environment at server start (verified with env -i); they are exempt (TMUX_OWN_GLOBALS). The operator's tmux.conf runs TPM, which set-environment -g's TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH on every fresh fork; it is removed and named like any other variable on the next restart (seen in phase A). The log wording was generalised to 'from the private tmux server environment that panes may not inherit' because of it.

show-environment -g parsing: bash exported functions (production has BASH_FUNC__aws%%) print multi-line values whose continuation lines start with a space or '}'; an entry is a line starting `NAME=` with NAME matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_%]*; -NAME markers are skipped (production already has -DISPATCH_TOKEN, -GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64, -GH_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64 from the 06:10 mitigation, so those two names will NOT appear in the production scrub log; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, LEGION_OMP_PATH, OMP_SESSION_ID, JJ_CONFIG, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE, GIT_CONFIG_*, TMUX, TMUX_PANE and ~60 operator-shell names will).

checkpoint 13 inspects the server's own /proc/<pid>/environ, which is fork-time: a hand-forked stale server fails it by construction even after the scrub (phase A: 'pid 990713 environ carries GH_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64='), and down.sh refuses to kill a session without @legion_owner. Both documented in the README; phase B (daemon-forked) is the green run.

Reusing SMOKE_DIR for phase B: boot never resurrects trees, so the daemon-forked server appeared only at the first resync (T+10 min); two roots resurrecting concurrently raced on the first new-session (see observations).

Scrub ordering: it runs AFTER `await probes` (a definitive probe negative must stay the first and only runner call) and before enableLaunches(); a tmux failure reading/writing either table is fatal exactly like a probe failure.

tmux 3.7c session-table facts (scratch server, verified): a fresh session's table is only the -NAME markers of the default update-environment list; an `attach` copies the client's SSH_ASKPASS/SSH_AUTH_SOCK/SSH_CONNECTION in (and the operator's DISPLAY etc. when set); `set-option -t <session> update-environment ''` makes a later attach copy nothing; `set-environment -t <session> -u NAME` removes the entry and a pane created afterwards no longer carries it; `-u` on a -NAME marker exits 0; `show-environment -t`/`set-option -t`/`set-environment -t` on a missing session say `no such session: <name>` (exit 1).

Rebase: main gained #991 between my two CI runs; its new workerCatchup fixture (processes.test.ts:4072) lacked the now-required baseEnv, so GitHub's merge commit failed typecheck and #991's new test threw on the undefined spread while the branch itself stayed green. Rebased once onto main@origin (architect-authorised; the deployment rule forbids pointless reruns, and a red run must rerun regardless); no textual conflicts.
observationsForArchitect: Session-environment leak path (not in scope, not fixed): tmux's default `update-environment` copies SSH_AUTH_SOCK/SSH_CONNECTION/DISPLAY/... from an attaching client into the SESSION environment; the production private session already carries SSH_AUTH_SOCK and SSH_CONNECTION (tmux -L legion-sjawharlegion show-environment -t legion-sjawharlegion, names only) from operator attaches, and panes opened afterwards inherit the operator's SSH agent socket. The scrub covers the global table only. Remedy if wanted: `set-option -t legion-<project> update-environment ''` at session creation plus a session-table scrub - a separate change.

Pre-existing race (seen in phase B): two trees resurrected by one resync both saw has-session=false on a not-yet-forked server and both ran new-session; the second failed 'tmux new-session failed (exit 1)' and counted a launch failure. openWindow serialises per issue, not across issues, for session creation. Unrelated to this change; remedy: serialise session creation in TmuxRuntime across issues.

Same-uid /proc reads remain possible (spec Rejected already accepts this): a pane can read the daemon's or the old server's /proc/<pid>/environ. The old production server (pid 2023008) keeps the key material in its fork-time environ until it exits; rotation (acceptance 5) is what retires that material.
Full daemon suite: 1 unnamed failure in the first of 6 runs, during the rig's concurrent start at load average 110+; 5 clean runs. Likely a timing-sensitive e2e test; not reproduced.
